correctness.rationale: Let a=u/(u+d), E=exp(-pT), F=exp(-qT). Composing the two affine flows gives multiplier EF strictly between zero and one; the periodic light-start excess over a is (1-a)(1-F)/(1-EF). Its integrated illuminated contribution is that excess times (1-E)/(u+d), giving the stated J_c after dividing by T and charging c once per cycle. For an independent concavity check put R=g_p+g_q, g_s=coth(sT/2), so Phi=2/R. For each s>0, g_s'<0 and g_s g_s''-2(g_s')^2=2(s/2)^2 csch^2(sT/2)>0. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives RR''>2R sum((g_s')²/g_s)>=2(R')², hence Phi'>0 and Phi''<0. The analytic expansion R=2(1/p+1/q)/T+(p+q)T/6+O(T³) gives Phi=pq T/(p+q)-p²q² T³/[12(p+q)]+O(T⁵). Consequently H=Phi-T Phi' starts at zero with cubic coefficient p²q²/[6(p+q)], and H tends to one at infinity because Phi tends to one and T Phi' decays exponentially. Since H'=-T Phi''>0 and J_c'=(c-KH)/T², c=0 and c>=K give the claimed strictly monotone unattained boundary suprema, including the equality c=K. For 0<c<K the derivative switches sign once and gives the unique finite optimum. Substitution gives the strictly positive improvement K Phi'(T_c), monotonicity follows by inversion, and the cubic coefficient gives the reported small-cost law. The fast zero-cost limit fa+Kpq/(p+q) simplifies to the fraction in the statement. The result requires two phases of positive share and a positive dark repair rate; no interchange with a boundary limit in f or v is claimed. Inspected checker.py as text. Its finite diagnostics are not needed for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: This idealized model isolates a meaningful decision: whether paying a setup charge at each switch makes rapid cycling too costly and whether any best finite period remains. The threshold equals the total excess light-phase output available after complete dark repair in the long-cycle limit, which explains its invariance with fixed positive duty and dark repair. The uniqueness, endpoint behavior and singular cube-root onset give a precise benchmark for charged two-phase models. The cost is stipulated rather than physically estimated, so no claimed empirical, energetic or general control prescription is warranted.
